$$f_{n+1} = f_n + \tfrac{a - f_n^2}{2}.$$

$$f_{n+1} - s = f_n - s + \tfrac{s^2 - f_n^2}{2} = (f_n - s)\Big(1 - \tfrac{s+f_n}{2}\Big).$$
Since $f_n \le s \le 1$, we have $s + f_n \le 2$, so $1 - \frac{s+f_n}{2} \ge 0$, while $f_n - s \le 0$; hence $f_{n+1} - s \le 0$, i.e. $f_{n+1} \le s$. Thus $0 \le f_n \le s$ for all $n$, the sequence is increasing (since $f_{n+1} - f_n = \frac{s^2 - f_n^2}{2} \ge 0$), and bounded above by $s$, so it converges pointwise to some limit $\ell \in [0,s]$ satisfying $\ell = \ell + \frac{s^2 - \ell^2}{2}$, i.e. $\ell^2 = s^2$, $\ell = s = |x|$ (taking the nonnegative root). So $f_n(x) \to |x|$ pointwise.

**Step 2. Uniform convergence via an explicit error bound.**

Define the error $e_n(x) = |x| - f_n(x) = s - f_n \ge 0$, with $e_0 = s$. From the computation above,
$$e_{n+1} = e_n\Big(1 - \tfrac{s+f_n}{2}\Big).$$
Since $f_n = s - e_n$, this gives
$$e_{n+1} = e_n\Big(1 - \tfrac{2s - e_n}{2}\Big) = e_n(1 - s) + \tfrac{e_n^2}{2}. \tag{$\ast$}$$

First note $e_n \le s$ for all $n$ (since $f_n \ge 0$): base $e_0 = s$; if $e_n \le s$ then by $(\ast)$,
$$e_{n+1} \le e_n(1-s) + \tfrac{e_n \cdot s}{2} = e_n\Big(1 - \tfrac{s}{2}\Big) \le e_n \le s.$$
In fact the sharper recursion $e_{n+1} \le e_n(1 - s/2)$ holds, giving
$$e_n(s) \le s\Big(1 - \tfrac{s}{2}\Big)^n, \qquad s \in [0,1]. \tag{$\ast\ast$}$$

$$g_n'(s) = \Big(1 - \tfrac{s}{2}\Big)^{n-1}\Big[1 - \tfrac{(n+1)s}{2}\Big] = 0 \implies s_* = \tfrac{2}{n+1}.$$
The maximum value is
